item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00102","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C03","C19","C14"],"selected_candidate_label":"C03","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C03 is a highly plausible concrete template. Like the child, it terminates an earlier bilateral trade-agreement proclamation and, because that termination changes the applicable most-favored-nation treatment, correspondingly amends the tariff list governing Cuban preferences. The child closely reproduces C03's recital-to-operation sequence and its divided operative structure, while substituting Peru, ginger root, and an October 1951 effective date for Mexico, the affected products, and January 1951. C19 and C14 contain related termination-and-supplementation machinery, but neither matches this combined bilateral-termination/Cuban-rate-adjustment pattern as directly.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Whereas the termination of the said proclamation of June 29, 1942 ... will result in the reestablishment as the most-favored-nation rate ... and following such termination the rate of duty for such ginger root, the product of Cuba ... will be 18 per centum ad valorem","parent_excerpt":"Whereas I determine that, following the termination of the said trade agreement specified in the fifth recital ... the rates of duty for the following descriptions of products in the ninth recital of the said proclamation of January 1, 1948 ... are the rates specified below","explanation":"Both connect termination of a bilateral trade agreement to recalculation of Cuban preferential duties under the same 1948 Cuban proclamation."},{"child_excerpt":"PART I That said proclamation of June 29, 1942, relating to the said trade agreement with the Republic of Peru, shall be terminated in whole on October 7, 1951.","parent_excerpt":"PART I ... The said proclamations of December 28, and 31, 1942, relating to the said trade agreement with the United Mexican States, shall be terminated in whole as of the close of December 31, 1950.","explanation":"The operative termination provision uses materially parallel language and merely substitutes the country, underlying proclamations, and effective date."},{"child_excerpt":"PART II That the list set forth in the ninth recital of the said proclamation of January 1, 1948, as amended and rectified ... shall be further amended by changing the rate in item 778","parent_excerpt":"PART III To the end that the said exclusive trade agreement specified in the ninth recital of this proclamation may be carried out, the list set forth in the ninth recital of the said proclamation of January 1, 1948, as amended and rectified, shall on and after January 1, 1951, be further amended in the manner indicated in the eleventh recital","explanation":"Both follow the termination with amendment of the same ninth-recital Cuban tariff list, providing the clearest shared administrative machinery."}]}
